content:
Knowledge recorded by Shinnecock elders in 2014

Blue-claw and lady crabs

Crabbing is described as long-standing Shinnecock work along the water’s edge. The entry distinguishes blue-claw crabs used for food, including their soft-shell stage, from lady crabs that were not usually eaten.1

Places named in the catalogue

Long Island Sound; Atlantic Ocean; Shinnecock Bay; Mecox Bay; Montauk Bay; Peconic Bay; Napeague Bay.1

Spider crabs

Spider crabs appear in the catalogue as inhabitants of shallow bays and deeper waters. Their inclusion broadens the record beyond the species most familiar from commercial seafood.2

Places named in the catalogue

Long Island Sound; Atlantic Ocean; Shinnecock Bay; Mecox Bay; Montauk Bay; Peconic Bay; Napeague Bay.2

Page references

The Shinnecock Environmental Department compiled this catalogue from elders’ memories and community resource knowledge in 2014. Food and medicine appear here as historical knowledge; safe identification and treatment require current guidance.

Shinnecock Environmental Department, Natural Resources Identified by Shinnecock Elders, April 4, 2014, PDF pp. 4–5. Page numbers count the cover as PDF page 1.
